body: For all the cases like these I left the default value as is, in most cases the square of the actual value isn't representable (`1e40` is smaller than the smallest value representable by `float`)
There are a few cases like this across the code base that make no sense, didn't change it in this case but would consider removing them as they are never true

These can all probably be replaced with:

But left them as is for now to reduce the changes
*larger than the largest value representable by `float` (about 3.4e38)

This is promoting to 64 bits I think?
Should probably be `64` or `64.0f'.

See #57703 for more details and why we need cleanup PRs from time to time.

Changing this in this way has potential to cause bugs as you are changing behaviour?

Probably left for separate PR.

Generally the point of these values is to be "effectively infinity" so that all other values are below it, so larger values should generally be better. I wonder if there's any reason to not use infinity itself? Otherwise, `FLT_MAX` is the constant to use.
